headline: A joint FBI, CISA, and South Korean advisory warns that Gunra ransomware is breaching critical infrastructure worldwide through Fortinet and Schneider Electric flaws, as Poland reveals hackers shut a heat plant's turbine by slipping in over a private cellular network.

emerging_trends.text: OpenAI's release of GPT-5.6-Cyber, a model trained to hunt zero-days and build exploit chains with far fewer refusals, shows vendors arming vetted defenders with frontier offensive power even as the coming Astra model threatens a critical autonomous-attack threshold.

Attackers keep moving command-and-control onto decentralized rails, with the Aeternum loader routing through Polygon smart contracts and Kimwolf v7 resolving its controllers through Ethereum ENS and Tor to resist takedown.

State-backed crews are industrializing their tradecraft, as North Korea's Kimsuky runs AI offline on its own servers to automate malware development and Russia's Sandworm poses as recruiters to snare Ukrainian IT workers.

topics.title: Gunra Ransomware Hits Critical Infrastructure Worldwide
topics.latest_developments: The FBI, CISA, and South Korea's National Police Agency published joint advisory AA26-222a on August 10, 2026, warning that Gunra affiliates breach networks by exploiting flaws in popular Fortinet and Schneider Electric products.
topics.summary: Gunra is a ransomware-as-a-service operation that surfaced in 2025, moved to an affiliate model in 2026, and runs double extortion against healthcare, financial services, government, and nonprofit targets. Agencies urge organizations to patch exposed Fortinet and Schneider Electric gear and harden internet-facing systems.

topics.title: Polish Heat Plant Breached Through Private APN
topics.latest_developments: CERT Polska disclosed that a December 29, 2025 attack on a Polish combined heat and power plant marked the first observed case of intruders reaching an operational technology network through a private APN, the dedicated cellular link the local grid operator uses to reach remote equipment.
topics.summary: The attackers shut down a steam turbine and the process-water treatment system at a plant supplying heat to roughly 50,000 residents, with recovery starting around 7:30 a.m. while they remained inside the network. The same day, coordinated attacks struck more than 30 other renewable installations and a larger heat plant.

topics.title: OpenAI Ships GPT-5.6-Cyber Offensive Model
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI unveiled GPT-5.6-Cyber, a model built on GPT-5.6 Sol and trained to find zero-days and build exploit chains with fewer refusals on dual-use work, releasing it only through the Daybreak Red tier of its vetted partner program, which the company expanded on August 10, 2026.
topics.summary: Approved red-team partners get the models while their clients receive only the findings, and OpenAI assigns the current GPT-5.6-Sol a 'high' cyber threat rating. Researchers warn the upcoming Astra model could reach the maximum 'critical' autonomous-attack threshold.

topics.title: Nation-State Crews Automate Espionage
topics.latest_developments: South Korean firm Genians found North Korea's Kimsuky now running AI offline on its own servers to power phishing and malware development, CERT-UA tied a recruiter-impersonation campaign against Ukrainian IT workers running since May to Russia's GRU-linked Sandworm, and Kaspersky detailed Project CAV3RN hitting Israel with Google Apps Script command-and-control relays.
topics.summary: Kimsuky connects document-search tools to its own files and gathers parts to build AI into malware, Sandworm poses as recruiters to lure Ukrainian technical staff, and the modular .NET NativeAOT CAV3RN framework hides its traffic inside legitimate Google services. All three target adversary governments and critical sectors.

topics.title: Blockchain-Based Botnet C2 Spreads
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 published back-to-back teardowns of two botnets that anchor command-and-control on public blockchains: the Aeternum loader, which routes through Polygon smart contracts, and Kimwolf v7, which resolves its controllers through Ethereum ENS with Tor as a backup while running HTTP/2 DDoS fingerprinting against Android IoT devices.
topics.summary: Both operations use decentralized infrastructure that survives domain and server takedowns because no single provider can pull the C2 offline. Defenders should watch for outbound connections to blockchain RPC endpoints and ENS resolvers from IoT and endpoint fleets.

sources.title: The Permanent Threat: Analyzing Aeternum's Blockchain-Based C2 Operations and Communications
Kimwolf v7: An Evolution of the Kimwolf Botnet

topics.title: BdThemes Supply-Chain Hack Spawns Rogue WordPress Admins
topics.latest_developments: Wordfence researcher Paolo Tresso reported that a threat actor compromised the upstream infrastructure of premium WordPress plugin vendor BdThemes and altered a remote JSON feed delivered to administrators' browsers so it silently creates rogue admin accounts, prompting the WordPress.org plugins team to disable the downloads.
topics.summary: The attack modified no source files in the official WordPress.org repository, instead poisoning data the plugins fetch at runtime, which defeats traditional code-scanning defenses. Sites running BdThemes tools should audit for unrecognized administrator accounts.

business_politics.title: Oil Jumps as Hormuz Talks Stall
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude touched $90 a barrel on August 11 as talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz hit an impasse and President Trump said Iran must pay compensation before any deal.
business_politics.summary: Iran's hardened demands and a stalled U.S. negotiation have kept the Strait of Hormuz closed, pulling millions of barrels of refined fuel off global markets; Treasury yields and the dollar climbed alongside crude as investors priced a prolonged energy shock and fresh doubt about the Federal Reserve's response.
